item.title: Best fantasy football waiver wire pickups: 12 players to add for NFL Week 10
item.description: Trades, injuries and byes make things difficult for fantasy managers this week. Here are a dozen players trending upwards who might be able to help.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline has arrived and there will no doubt be plenty of action down to the wire.

Fantasy football managers have a bit more time to assemble the final puzzle pieces for a championship roster via the trade market. But the possibility of being stuck with lineup holes for Week 10 is still a valid concern.

Another four teams are on bye this week, nixing the availability of ... well, Bo Nix, as well as Caleb Williams, D'Andre Swift, Luther Burden, Bucky Irving, Saquon Barkley, Jonah Coleman and many others.

After another round of devastating injuries, who might be out there on the waiver wire this week?

ON BYE: Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia, Tampa Bay

Fantasy football players to add for Week 10

Due to the wide variance in types of leagues and individual team needs, the players listed here include their availability in Yahoo leagues, which may or may not match roster rates on other platforms. Suggested bid values based on $100 free agent acquisition budget (FAAB) for the season.

For customized waiver wire suggestions, synced to your league and subscribe to USA TODAY Sports Fantasy's exclusive tools.

RB Kaleb Johnson, Green Bay Packers (2% rostered)

Starter Josh Jacobs is likely out for an extended period due to a broken finger, leaving Johnson as the top healthy running back in Green Bay this week. Of course, the Packers have the NFL's worst rushing offense this season so temper your expectations. Johnson did get into the end zone in Week 9, so there is a possibility history can repeat itself, even if it's against a tough Vikings defense. (Recommended FAAB bid: $12)

WR Jordan Watkins, San Francisco 49ers (2% rostered)

Someone has to catch passes from Brock Purdy, and with WRs Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel sidelined, Watkins stepped forward to pull in all four of his targets for 86 yards and a touchdown. With a matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on tap and uncertainty surrounding the availability of Evans and Samuel (not to mention recently reinstated Brandon Aiyuk), Watkins seems like the best receiving option outside of TE George Kittle. (FAAB bid: $8)

WRs Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte, Houston Texans (14%/5% rostered)

Coming off a five-TD showing against the Chargers, QB C.J. Stroud seems to be firing on all cylinders. And he's spreading the wealth among his receivers. Xavier Hutchinson (1% rostered) was the top recommendation of the bunch last week − and he did catch a touchdown pass − but so did Dell, Boutte and Nico Collins. Heck, this week it could be Marvin Harrison Jr.'s turn to shine. Regardless, you want a piece of this offense this week at Cleveland. (FAAB bids: $7 each, with $5 on Hutchinson as a backup.)

RB Audric Estime, New Orleans Saints (5% rostered)

The Saints cut the cord on RB Kendre Miller this past week and reacquired Estime to team with Alvin Kamara. He jumped right back into the mix with a healthy 15 carries for 72 yards and a touchdown. Estime played 35 snaps, compared to Kamara's 37, but was clearly the lead back with Kamara only getting six carries and playing mostly on passing downs. (FAAB bid: $6)

RB Seth McGowan, Indianapolis Colts (33% rostered)

McGowan scored his first NFL touchdown against the Cowboys on Sunday, but could have an even larger role if Jonathan Taylor gets traded. Fantasy managers will know his status by their waiver wire deadline, so bid accordingly. Even if Taylor stays put, McGowan will still have a role. (FAAB bid: $5 if Taylor stays, $20+ if Taylor is dealt)

RB Justice Hill, Baltimore Ravens (5% rostered)

There's no question Derrick Henry is the Ravens' top back. However, the quarterbck situation with Jacoby Brissett now running the show doesn't inspire a lot of confidence. Henry will get his touches, but his greatest value comes as a battering Raven late in the game when they have the lead. It's more likely Baltimore will be playing catch-up, which puts Hill on the field much more frequently. (FAAB bid: $5)

TE AJ Barner, Seattle Seahawks (10% rostered)

The wheel of tight ends spins again ... and this past week, it landed on Barner. He's only had one game with more than five targets, but he caught one in the end zone against the Cardinals. However, Barner's greatest value lies in his role as the quarterback when Seattle lines up in the Tush Push formation. He added a 1-yard TD run to his stat line on Sunday and finsihed as the TE5 for the week. (FAAB bid: $4)

WRs Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell, Los Angeles Rams (2% rostered)

How to replace Puka Nacua? The short answer is, you can't. Perhaps the Rams will turn more toward the running game with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. But when QB Matthew Stafford has to throw, he'll need receivers on the other end. Mumpfield had a great game in Week 3 (4-93, TD), but has done little since. Atwell has caught seven passes all season. (Perhaps the Rams will make a trade for a wideout.) Don't go overboard just because these guys are wearing the blue and gold. (FAAB bid: $3)

QB Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh Steelers (34% rostered)

The quarterback position could be an absolute mess this week (and perhaps beyond). From backups becoming starters to familiar faces starting in new places, you won't find too many easy decisions. Rodgers has been pretty consistent the season, and he'll be coming off his bye against the Bengals. (FAAB bid: $3)

WR Pat Bryant, Denver Broncos (3% rostered)

Just activated after spending four weeks on injured reserve with an ankle injury, Bryant made an immediate impact on Sunday, catching four passes for 56 yards and a score. The Broncos are on bye this week so consider him a deep-league stash if you have roster space. (FAAB bid: $1)

item.title: Seattle Seahawks 2026 trade deadline tracker
item.description: Follow ongoing coverage of the 2026 NFL trade deadline, including whether or not the Seahawks make one more move.
item.content:encoded:
We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. Minor or mid-level deals have happened more recently on deadline day itself, so it’s not like we live in a “nothing happens” world. There have admittedly been prominent in-season trades already this year, including the Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons trades just a couple of weeks ago, as well as Joey Porter Jr going to the Dallas Cowboys, and Marvin Harrison Jr heading for the Houston Texans.

For the second year in a row, the trade deadline is during Week 10. The Seattle Seahawks are usually active during the deadline, and this year they’ve pulled off one major trade. Will John Schneider cook up another midseason masterclass like he did for Leonard Williams, Quandre Diggs, Carlos Dunlap, and other names from previous deadline deals? Follow Field Gulls’ trade tracker coverage throughout Monday and Tuesday, and we’ll see what the Seahawks will do as they look to get back on track after a sputtering 5-4 start.

Have the Seattle Seahawks made any trades during the regular season?

Yes. They acquired longtime Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder.

Who could the Seahawks potentially put on the trade block?

No one immediately springs to mind. The likes of Dante Fowler Jr have rarely played this year but likely wouldn’t fetch much on the trade market. Emanuel Wilson being an unofficial healthy scratch is worth monitoring, although similarly he’s not much of a valuable trade piece, and Seattle may not want to risk moving any capable RB given the injury concerns on the depth chart.

Which positions would the Seahawks potentially be most interested in?

Edge rusher and wide receiver might be two positions of need for Seattle. Rashid Shaheed’s injury and generally underwhelming receiving stats could impact what Seattle does at receiver. The edge rushing room is essentially three deep, and with only Derick Hall and Connor O’Toole under contract beyond 2027, there might be some forward thinking required. The New York Jets’ Will McDonald IV has reportedly requested a trade and could be one to watch.

When does the NFL trade deadline window close?

At 4 pm ET/1 pm PT on Tuesday, Nov. 10.

Latest Seattle Seahawks trade news

Notable NFL trade news (Nov. 10)

  • The Eagles are trading pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals for a 2027 sixth-round pick.

Notable NFL trade news (Nov. 9)

  • WHOA! The Jaguars just traded for Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis, giving up a 2027 first-rounder and a 2029 second.
  • The Atlanta Falcons have traded safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-rounder and a 2028 fifth-rounder.
  • The New York Jets have dealt safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth-rounder.
  • The New Orleans Saints have agreed to trade defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2028 sixth-rounder, which could become a 2027 sixth-rounder.

item.title: 2026 NFL trade deadline tracker: Grades, analysis and details from every key deal
item.description: We'll be tracking and grading the trades across the NFL up until the Nov. 10 deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade market is open with several high-profile deals already done. We'll be tracking and grading the key trades across the NFL up until Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline.

Eagles trade EDGE Arnold Ebiketie to Bengals

  • Date: Nov. 10

Bengals receive: EDGE Arnold Ebiketie

Eagles receive: 2027 sixth-round draft pick

Eagles trade DT Jordan Davis to Jaguars

  • Date: Nov. 9

Jaguars receive: DT Jordan Davis

Grade: B+

Eagles receive: 2027 first-round draft pick and 2029 second-round pick

Grade: A-

The Jaguars left no doubt they're going for a Super Bowl this year by making their third trade of the day, following deals for Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux. Davis was the biggest move of them all as Jacksonville paid a robust price for a big run-stopping tackle who can plug into the middle of the defense. The Eagles signed Davis to a three-year, $78 million extension in March, yet Davis' cap hit for 2027 is a very reasonable figure at just over $8.5 million.

For the Eagles, it's a tough short-term pill to swallow for the franchise and a fan base used to competing every season, but the long-term payoff could be immense. The Eagles' to-do list this offseason grows, but the potential of how they can reshape the roster is equally as exciting. — Eric Edholm

Jets trade safety Andre Cisco to Lions

  • Date: Nov. 9

Lions receive: S Andre Cisco

Jets receive: 2028 sixth-round draft pick

Saints trade DT Davon Godchaux to Jaguars

  • Date: Nov. 9

Jaguars receive: DT Devon Godchaux

Saints receive: Conditional 2028 sixth-round draft pick

Falcons trade safety Jessie Bates to Jaguars

  • Date: Nov. 9

Jaguars receive: S Jessie Bates

Grade: B+

Falcons receive: 2027 second-round draft pick and 2028 fifth-round pick

Grade: A-

Safety flew beneath the radar a bit for Jacksonville, but injuries made it a position of some concern. Bates has a lot of qualities that fit the Jaguars seek. He's one of the league's better center fielders — and he's a ballhawk. It comes at a cost, however. Bates is set to hit free agency, and given the team's tight cap situation, he could end up being a half-season rental.

Bates is the ideal type of asset to trade off in this situation, given his expiring contract and reaching a point in his career where his value might start to depreciate. Getting back a plum draft pick for an expiring contract made it well worth the price. — Eric Edholm

Cardinals trade QB Jacoby Brissett to Ravens

  • Date: Nov. 4

Ravens receive: QB Jacoby Brissett and 2027 fifth-round draft pick

Grade: B-

Cardinals receive: 2027 fourth-round draft pick and 2028 seventh-round pick

Grade: C+

Nobody should believe Brissett will save Baltimore's season and help it win a division. But he was the best option available, and he at least makes sure the Ravens aren't playing out the string with uncompetitive football for two months. And maybe a miracle happens and the Ravens are still in contention by the time Lamar Jackson returns, if he can this season.

It's a reasonable move for the Cardinals, who are going to start rookie Carson Beck soon to get a look at him by next season. Gardner Minshew can do as well as Brissett in the short term. They get to add draft capital for a player who wasn't going to see the field the rest of the season and has an expiring contract. — Frank Schwab

Titans trade defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to Bears

  • Date: Oct. 29

Bears receive: DT Jeffery Simmons, 2028 first-round draft pick

Grade: B

Titans receive: 2027 first-round draft pick, 2027 fourth-round draft pick, 2028 fifth-round draft pick

Grade: A-

Value-wise, this is close to as much compensation as you'll see moved for a defensive player. But if the Bears make a Super Bowl run, the price very well could make the move a smart one. This trade sends a clear signal that the Bears are going for it all this season.

The Titans are facing a multi-year rebuild, and this was the best way to help starting toward that effort. They have more needs today than they did yesterday, and picks are merely lottery tickets, but this felt like a deal GM Mike Borgonzi had to make. – Eric Edholm

Colts trade guard Quenton Nelson to Seahawks

  • Date: Oct. 27

Seahawks receive: G Quenton Nelson

Grade: B+

Colts receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick

Grade: C+

The Colts have other players who are far less tethered to the organization who also soon could be moved. Lacking a first-round draft pick next year from the Sauce Gardner trade, the Colts are trying to recoup as much draft-pick value as possible before the spring. With Daniel Jones' struggles, along with the Colts' apparent lack of trust in Anthony Richardson Sr., the team almost certainly will be going QB hunting in the offseason. …

Given the stage of his career and his contract status, this could end up being a fairly pricy rental for the Seahawks — and that potential cost must be baked into the team's grade. But if Nelson plays to his expected level, or even above the level he's played at this season, and the Seahawks remain a title contender, it would be hard to label this as anything but a win. – Eric Edholm

Colts trade defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to 49ers

  • Date: Oct. 27

49ers receive: DT DeForest Buckner

Grade: A-

Colts receive: 2027 fourth-round pick

Grade: B-

The 49ers needed defensive help up front, and Buckner looks like the right-shaped peg for their hole inside. Osa Odighizuwa has supplied some pressure, and rookie Gracen Halton has had some big moments, but they're the only Niners DTs to play every game. There weren't many other dependable pieces inside. It was also a group that lacked length and the ability to close down passing lanes. Odighizuwa and Halton have the only two batted passes for the team this season. …

The Colts got about what could be expected in return, and considering how depleted their draft-pick drawer is with no first-round pick next year, every pick counts. Even with the 2027 selections they got for Nelson and Buckner likely falling closer to the ends of those respective rounds, the Colts are accumulating more immediate assets to compete for a quarterback next year. It's smarter than waiting a year for compensatory-pick value, even if they're having to pay for past sins. – Eric Edholm

Cardinals trade receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to Texans

  • Date: Oct. 12

Texans receive: WR Marvin Harrison Jr., 2027 sixth-round pick

Grade: C-

Cardinals receive: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pick

Grade: B-

Nobody outbid the Houston Texans for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. Whether that's a win for the Texans remains to be seen.

The Texans landed Harrison, the disappointing receiver from the Arizona Cardinals. It was reported Oct. 10 that the Cardinals were finalizing details on a trade for Harrison, but no team was announced. No team made a better offer to the Cardinals at the last minute, so Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round pick go to Houston for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick.

It gives Harrison a second chance. And Arizona recoups some value after a draft whiff on Harrison. – Frank Schwab

Ravens acquire center Cam Jurgens from Eagles

  • Date: Oct. 7

Ravens receive: C Cam Jurgens, 2027 seventh-round pick

Grade: B

Eagles receive: 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Grade: C+

The timing, one day after longtime Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly announced his retirement, is perhaps the most surprising element of the trade.

The Ravens, who have had a hard time replacing Tyler Linderbaum at center, recently watched as Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic all suffered injuries, forcing 2026 first-rounder Vega Ioane over from guard to center.

Jurgens now figures to be Baltimore's center for multiple seasons, given the nature of his contract after he signed an extension last year. – Eric Edholm

Cowboys acquire CB Joey Porter from Steelers

Date: Oct. 1

Cowboys receive: CB Joey Porter

Grade: B-

Steelers receive: 2027 sixth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Grade: B

Jerry Jones said before the season that he was itching to make another big trade.

The Dallas Cowboys owner made a move, with room to possibly make another splash before the deadline. Dallas dealt a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for their young cornerback Joey Porter Jr., a second-round selection in 2023.

It wasn't the all-in move Jones has teased. But it's still a big move that should help improve a defense that hasn't been great to start the 2026 season. – Frank Schwab

Giants trade for Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy

  • Date: Sept. 28

Giants receive: QB J.J. McCarthy

Grade: B-

Vikings receive: 2027 fifth-round pick

Grade: D

Is J.J. McCarthy, who fell from first- to third-string quarterback quickly in Minnesota, the answer for a Giants team that lost not only Jaxson Dart but also its top pass rusher in All-Pro Brian Burns (season-ending ACL tear)? How quickly can McCarthy acclimate to a new offense, new terminology and new cast of supporting teammates?

McCarthy played and started 10 games in two-plus seasons as a Viking, winning an impressive six. But that record often reflected the talent around him and even moreso, the strength of the Vikings' defense.

McCarthy threw 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in his 10 Vikings games. Since he was drafted in 2024, his 72.6 passer rating ranks 43rd out of 44 quarterbacks who have started at least 10 games. Only Anthony Richardson Sr., whom the Indianapolis Colts tried and failed to trade in the spring, has posted a lower mark. — Frank Schwab (grades) and Jori Epstein

Cowboys acquire offensive tackle Broderick Jones from Steelers

  • Date: Aug. 29 

Cowboys receive: OL Broderick Jones, 2027 fourth-round pick

Grade: C-

Steelers receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2027 seventh-round pick

Grade: B

There was excitement for the Pittsburgh Steelers when they drafted Georgia offensive tackle Broderick Jones with the 14th overall NFL Draft pick in 2023. They even traded up to take him.

The excitement ran out when the Steelers traded Jones to the Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys sent a third- and sixth-round pick to the Steelers for Jones and a fourth-round pick.

Jones had dealt with a neck injury and had not been the player the Steelers thought they were getting. He had struggled to become a reliable tackle. He was in the mix to start for the Steelers this season but when Max Iheanachor, this year's first-round pick by Pittsburgh, made his preseason debut Thursday then Jones became expendable.

For the Cowboys, it's one of the chances they often take on players who were graded highly coming out of college but didn't work out with their first team.

– Frank Schwab

Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, and we've got the NFL trade deadline on deck, which is set for Tuesday afternoon at 4 p.m. ET. Buckle up!

The Colts also remain a team to watch ahead of the trade deadline, with star running back Jonathan Taylor at the crux of it all. Another team to watch is the Minnesota Vikings, whose need for a quarterback was apparent as ever as Carson Wentz struggled to find any rhythm on offense in Monday night’s loss to the Buffalo Bills. item.title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Will the Titans make any more moves?
item.description: The clock is ticking on the 2026 NFL trade deadline
item.content:encoded:
The Tennessee Titans already made the biggest move of the 2026 NFL trade deadline when they sent Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears for two first round picks. That deal was made a week and a half before the deadline. It felt like that was just the beginning of moves Mike Borgonzi would be making.

Now, we sit just hours from the deadline, and the Titans have not made another move. There have been plenty of rumors surrounding guys like Amani Hooker, Tony Pollard, and Calvin Ridley, but to this point, those guys are all still in Nashville. That begs the question: Is Borgonzi done?

Let’s take a look at the rumored players and see what makes sense as we approach today’s deadline:

Amani Hooker

Hooker is the most valuable of the three players who have been subject to rumors. He is coming off a 3-interception game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Yesterday, I asked on Twitter if you would trade Hooker for a second round pick. As of this writing, almost 77% said they would. Hooker is just 28 years old and playing at a high level. Borgonzi would probably need two picks, with one of them being on day 2, to move him.

Tony Pollard

Speaking of guys playing at a high level, Pollard is currently playing his best football as a Titan. He has 5 touchdowns in the Titans’ last two games. The reports out there suggest that Borgonzi doesn’t want to move him because he is important to Cam Ward’s development. That makes sense, but if he can get a fourth round pick or better for an aging running back, he needs to make that move.

The thing that complicates this deal a little further is that there are a few running backs rumored to be available. Jonathan Taylor is at the top of the list. The rumors are the Indianapolis Colts are going to move him. Teams could be waiting to see that deal go down before making their best and final offer to the Titans.

Calvin Ridley

This one is easy to me. If a team calls and offers a pick, any pick, for Ridley, the Titans should take it. He isn’t going to be here after this year, and he hardly gets on the field as it is. When he does get on the field, he beats up every pass that is thrown his direction.

item.title: Early Week 10 NFL betting, odds: 2 wagers that I like right now
item.description: Our NFL handicapper gives two Week 10 bets he likes at the moment.
item.content:encoded:
Something I have written about before and will continue to repeat: studying injury reports and accurately predicting which way major news will break is the biggest edge in sports betting right now.

Models and algorithms have gotten so sophisticated. The ability to price rest disparities, travel situations and motivation angles — common tropes among handicappers — are pretty easy to backtest, weight and reflect into the current odds. Often people say simply taking the best odds in the market and having multiple places to bet is the biggest edge. In my opinion, the biggest edge is collecting all the information regarding a players’ potential availability and pricing the probability he plays or not.

The bettors and the oddsmakers are on a relatively even playing field here in terms of access to information. Whether it comes from coach and player interviews, beat reporters’ eyes and ears, practice videos or any other source, this information is out in the public and the ability to react to it is paramount. Star players dealing with ailments that lead to uncertainty on their playing status are going to cause such significant line movements that a bettor can always take the worst odds in the market and still gain huge edges by being right.

This week, amidst trade deadline talk and hitting the midseason point, my focus is on the injury report. Here are two early bets I like in Week 10.

Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens (-5, 38.5)

From preseason priors to current form, this is the worst possible Monday Night Football scenario we could have imagined as fans as the 0-8 LA Chargers visit the 4-5 Baltimore Ravens. Lamar Jackson is out for the season, Tyler Huntley is out with turf toe and Baltimore just acquired Jacoby Brissett in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals to become the immediate starting QB. On the Chargers side, Justin Herbert is dealing with an injury to his middle finger on his left hand that may cause him to be sidelined as well, meaning rookie DJ Uiagalelei would take over.

The betting market has signaled so far that Justin Herbert will not play. The opening line was Baltimore Ravens -3.5 and it has been moved out to -5. This line will continue to move further out if Herbert is inactive, closer to Ravens -7, or it will be kicked back to Ravens -3 if Herbert does play.

My opinion here is that Herbert will play. The injury is a finger on his non throwing arm and the Monday X-rays came back negative. Herbert said, “Whatever I can do to be 100%, I am going to do,” and head coach Jim Harbaugh noted that Herbert “should be good to go.” This is a promising signal that Herbert will play, and some -5.5s already got kicked back to -4.5.

We have already seen Saints QB Tyler Shough play through broken bones on his non-throwing hand earlier this season. He was handing the ball off with his “good” hand despite the play design typically going the other direction. Washington Commanders QB Jayden Daniels came back quickly from a dislocated elbow on his non-throwing arm and is playing through the injury with a bulky brace. Those two injuries are relevant because they impacted the QB’s non-throwing arm, but also because both teams are really struggling and are more or less out of playoff contention already.

I will back Herbert to play and say this line closes near Chargers +3, so there is value on the +5 right now.

Bet: Chargers +5

San Francisco 49ers (-4, 55.5) at Dallas Cowboys

The Cowboys had two key late scratches before their Week 9 game against the Indianapolis Colts, as both WR George Pickens and CB Joey Porter Jr. were ruled out. Pickens is dealing with a hamstring injury while Porter Jr. is having ankle issues.

I had actually bet the Colts +5.5 on Saturday last week and factored them both at 80% or higher to play despite perhaps being limited in snap count or ability. Neither Pickens nor Porter Jr. missed a single practice last week; Pickens was limited in each and Porter was full in one practice and limited in the others. Cowboys head coach Brain Schottenheimer said he was hopeful both would play. They were late scratches, the line closed at Colts +3.5 and the Cowboys won by 4. It was a perfect encapsulation that betting before the news and getting on the right side of line movement really matters.

This week, I expect both players to play. The market remains unsure, but with the upgrade in opponent and another week to get in limited practice, I suspect both will go this Sunday. If that is the case, the Cowboys will close +3 here, and grabbing the +4 before and winning on the key number represents a large early week value add.

The 49ers are likely to get WR Deebo Samuel back, but I don’t expect them to get WR Mike Evans healthy for this game. With Samuel, Pickens and Porter Jr as the key injuries, getting these right is the biggest factor in handicapping this game for closing line value.

Bet: Cowboys +4

item.title: Report: Dolphins DT Zach Sieler to have season-ending biceps surgery
item.description: The Dolphins will reportedly be without one of their top defensive players for the rest of the season.
item.content:encoded:
The Dolphins will reportedly be without one of their top defensive players for the rest of the season.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that defensive tackle Zach Sieler tore his biceps early in Sunday's loss to the Lions. He was able to play the rest of the game, but needs to have surgery that will end his season.

Sieler started the first eight games of the season for the Dolphins. He had 24 tackles and two sacks in those appearances. He joined the team during the 2019 season and has 377 tackles, 37.5 sacks, two interceptions, five forced fumbles and six fumble recoveries during his time in Miami.

Sieler signed a three-year extension with the Dolphins ahead of the 2025 season. The deal ties him to the team through the 2029 season with cap hits of more than $20 million each year.

item.title: 3-Point Stance: Patriots’ trade deadline isn’t time for a youth movement
item.description: New England shouldn’t rush into midseason roster changes
item.content:encoded:
Are the New England Patriots sellers at the NFL trade deadline?

On Nov. 1, Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer highlighted defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Carlton Davis as potential Patriots trade candidates ahead of Tuesday’s deadline at 4 p.m. According to Breer, if a deal is struck, New England’s motivation would be centered around adding draft capital and transitioning into a younger roster.

As of Nov. 4, head coach Mike Vrabel appeared to disagree with that approach.

“I think sometimes national reports have the tendency to do that. I have not shared that information with anybody,” Vrabel said. “This time of year, I think that all these things kind of get drummed up. So, we’re focused on trying to prepare for [the Green Bay Packers] and make the corrections from [the week before].

“This is business as normal here, so I don’t know where a lot of these things come from. Certainly not from any conversations with me.”

However, does Vrabel and Co.’s stance about handling the trade deadline change after New England’s brutal 45-27 loss at the hands of the Packers on Sunday?

Vrabel offered a simple response when making an appearance on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show: “No.”

“We want a bunch of guys that want to be here,” he added. “That want to make it hard on each other. In preparation, push each other, challenge each other, improve, take accountability, and if that’s not them, then let us know by tomorrow. That’s what we have to do. That’s the mindset.”

And from a selling standpoint, his ruling could make sense as a final decision.

Regardless of whether or not the Patriots strike a deal involving either Barmore or Davis, trading almost any impact contributor on the roster while sitting at a 5-4 record at the regular season’s midway point, especially in the AFC, is certainly questionable. Both players were also members of the tight-knit group that made a Super Bowl appearance just nine months ago.

At the least, a deal of that stature calls for a corresponding “buying” move.

Sure, New England’s depth in multiple areas will be a largely discussed topic throughout the offseason regarding the team’s roster-building process. And rightfully so.

Vrabel said it himself after a preseason victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, stating at the time that he doesn’t think his team is “very deep.”

But six 2027 day-three draft picks make finding immediate, injury-relieving depth manageable. Sending away either Barmore or Davis simply doesn’t make sense at this time. Especially for a franchise still technically in contention for the AFC East title.

Trading Barmore creates another need

In 2023, Barmore posted his best season as a pro, recording 8.5 sacks, 16 quarterback hits and pressuring those passers 49 times. He also consistently disrupted opposing run offenses, forcing 13 tackles for a loss and totaling 64 combined takedowns.

That season-long performance earned the Patriots’ 2021 second-round draft selection a four-year, $84 million contract extension the following offseason.

Currently in year two of that new deal, Barmore’s production hasn’t entirely matched the monetary value of his contract, especially in run defense. From just last season, the 27-year-old has seen his involvement in that facet of the defense drop from 62.8% to just 36%.

Still, New England evidently continues to view Barmore as a producer when rushing the quarterback, heavily using the defensive tackle during pass-rush downs and critical third-down plays.

Barmore’s overall reduced role also doesn’t mean he’s expendable. Trading him shuffles the defensive line, forcing Cory Durden into a new, pass-rush-heavy role and 34-year-old DaQuan Jones, who has contributed as a relief piece for the primary starters, into a heavier workload.

Davis’ departure would leave a hole in the secondary

As for Davis, the cornerback hasn’t shown signs of regression. But the soon-to-be 30-year-old, entering the final year of his contract with a mighty injury history and owed $22 million in 2027, plays directly into the youth-movement argument.

Nonetheless, shipping him off to another franchise creates a glaring hole in the cornerback room. That decision then forces Vrabel and the defensive coaching staff to decide between starting substitute Charles Woods opposite Christian Gonzalez or pulling Marcus Jones away from his natural nickel-cornerback position.

With several offenses in the Patriots’ remaining schedule currently ranking top 10 in passing yards per game, that potential decision seems counterproductive.

Davis, who recently returned to the starting lineup last week after missing four games, played a significant role in New England’s divisional round victory against the Houston Texans in the playoffs last season, intercepting C.J. Stroud twice.

The offseason offers a better time to make a move

In Barmore’s case, an eventual deal appears likely. As the Boston Herald’s Andrew Callahan put it, the Patriots seemingly want “out of the Barmore business.”

On Friday, Breer wrote that the price for both Barmore and Davis “would likely” be around just a fourth-round selection.

An offseason deal, rather than a midseason trade, allows New England greater flexibility to reallocate resources and explore replacements to replicate or improve upon either player’s production while spending less.

The Patriots’ loss to Green Bay is concerning. Still, it’s not a season-ending sign.

It’s true that New England’s defense has struggled to deliver on the expectations surrounding their offseason additions of Dre’Mont Jones, All-Pro safety Kevin Byard and second-round pick Gabe Jacas. But much like the rest of the roster, that group has dealt with injuries.

The team’s matchup against the Miami Dolphins in Week Eight marked the first game the starting cornerback trio of Gonzalez, Davis and Jones all played together since Week Three.

Even though eventually moving Barmore or another established contributor makes sense for the team’s long-term roster construction, the Patriots’ timing of a potential trade should account for the franchise’s current position in the AFC playoff picture.

item.title: NFL trade deadline deal tracker includes Jessie Bates, Jacoby Brissett, and more
item.description: Tracking all the deals made ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is right around the corner. Teams have until 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, November 10, to make deals in an effort to either improve rosters for a playoff push, or prepare for a rebuild over the upcoming offseason.

But some teams have not waited to push deals across the line.

Monday began with the news that the Atlanta Falcons were sending defensive back Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars, as general manager James Gladstone tries to improve a defense that is already considered one of the best in the league.

While we expect more deals to come, here is a running list of the trades that have gone down so far. This will be updated as new deals come through.

Eagles trade Arnold Ebiketie to Bengals

The Eagles are not done making moves. On Tuesday, Philadelphia traded pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals, giving the AFC North contenders another presence on the edge.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Bengals receive: EDGE Arnold Ebiketie
  • Eagles receive: A 2027 sixth-round pick

Eagles trade Jordan Davis to Jaguars

The Jacksonville Jaguars are absolutely all-in on the 2026 season.

After acquiring both Jessie Bates III and Davon Godchaux earlier in the day, James Gladstone added yet another piece, trading for defensive tackle Jordan Davis in a deal with the Philadelphia Eagles.

Davis has tallied 31 tackles and 1.5 sacks this season, including a sack of J.J. McCarthy on Sunday in Philadelphia’s 19-11 loss to the New York Giants. The trade gives Anthony Campanile yet another talented player on the interior, and now Eagles general manager Howie Roseman has a pair of picks in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Jaguars receive: DT Jordan Davis
  • Eagles receive: A 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick

Jets trade Andre Cisco to Lions

The Detroit Lions are getting some help on defense.

The New York Jets are trading safety Andre Cisco to Detroit. The safety is on an expiring contract, and the Jets — who at the moment have more than $80 million in available cap space for next year — are getting what they can now.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Lions receive: S Andre Cisco
  • Jets receive: A 2028 sixth-round selection

Saints trade Davon Godchaux to Jaguars

The Jacksonville Jaguars are not done adding to their defense.

Hours after trading for safety Jessie Bates III, the Jaguars swung a deal with the New Orleans Saints to acquire defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. While Bates can patrol the deep third of the defense and gives defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile a flexible safety that can play both in the deep middle and down near that line of scrimmage, Godchaux gives Jacksonville another option along the defensive line. That is something the Jaguars needed to add after the team lost DaVon Hamilton for the season due to a torn quad.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Jaguars receive: DT Davon Godchaux
  • Saints receive: 2028 sixth-round pick (which could elevate to a 2027 sixth-round pick if Jacksonville acquires one via trade or the compensatory selection formula)

Falcons trade Jessie Bates III to Jaguars

Trade deadline week kicked off in style with the Atlanta Falcons sending veteran safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars. For the Jaguars, it is a move to shore up the secondary as Jacksonville tries to maximize the current window of contention. For Atlanta, it is a move to get something for Bates ahead of his free agency, and with the Falcons currently looking at over $100 million in cap space, they might not receive a compensatory selection for Bates should he walk in free agency and Atlanta make the most of those resources.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Jaguars receive: S Jessie Bates III
  • Falcons receive: A 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick

Cardinals trade Jacoby Brissett to Ravens

With Arizona benching quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and the Ravens suddenly looking at life without Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley for at least the next few weeks as both are dealing with injuries, this move makes a good bit of sense. Brissett gets a chance to play on a team that is trying to stay in the playoff chase, the Ravens get a quarterback that gives them a chance to do just that, and Arizona … well maybe they could have handled things differently but they got some picks in return.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Ravens receive: QB Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick
  • Cardinals receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick

Titans trade Jeffery Simmons to Bears

Now this was a big one.

With the Chicago Bears trying to keep pace in the tough NFC North, and the defense remaining an issue, general manager Ryan Poles swung for the fences, bringing in defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons in a trade with the Tennessee Titans. Simmons paid immediate dividends, as he was stellar in his Chicago debut against the Seattle Seahawks.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Bears receive: DL Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick
  • Titans receive: A 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick, and a 2027 fourth-round pick

Colts trade DeForest Buckner to 49ers

Changes are coming in Indianapolis.

After parting ways with general manager Chris Ballard, the Colts began moving players with an eye to the future. One of those deals saw Indianapolis send DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers, returning the defensive lineman to the team that drafted him with the seventh-overall pick in the 2016 NFL Draft.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • 49ers receive: DL DeForest Buckner
  • Colts receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick

Colts trade Quenton Nelson to Seahawks

Indianapolis started their impending fire sale with a move involving guard Quenton Nelson. Still one of the premier interior offensive linemen in the NFL, the Colts sent him to Seattle as the Seahawks look to shore up their offensive line.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Seahawks receive: IOL Quenton Nelson
  • Colts receive: A 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick

Cardinals trade Marvin Harrison Jr. to Texans

It just never seemed to click for Marvin Harrison Jr. in Arizona.

Billed as one of the top wide receiver prospects in recent memory, Harrison never quite lived up to that hype with the Cardinals. Arizona selected him as the fourth-overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, and after catching 62 passes for 885 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, he caught just 41 passes during 2025 and had only pulled in five receptions through the first four games of the season with Arizona.

In a move that reunited him with former college teammate C.J. Stroud, the Texans acquired him to try and give Stroud a familiar target in the passing game.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Texans receive: WR Marvin Harrison Jr. and a 2027 sixth-round pick
  • Cardinals receive: A 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 seventh-round pick

Eagles trade Cam Jurgens to Ravens

Back at the start of October, the Baltimore Ravens swung a deal for offensive lineman Cam Jurgens of the Eagles.

The move was made to shore up the interior offensive line, in the wake of center Tyler Linderbaum signing with the Las Vegas Raiders last offseason. Baltimore’s top three centers were on injured reserve at the time the move was made, and the Ravens were using rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane in the middle.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Ravens receive: IOL Cam Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick
  • Eagles receive: A 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick

Steelers trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys

October began with the Pittsburgh Steelers finally coming to a decision on cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Porter was seeking a contract extension from the team, but the two sides were unable to come to terms on a new deal. He also missed each of Pittsburgh’s first three games of the season due to a lingering back injury.

So Jerry Jones stepped in, acquiring the cornerback in yet another move to try and shore up a struggling defense.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Cowboys receive: CB Joey Porter Jr.
  • Steelers receive: A 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick

Vikings trade J.J. McCarthy to Giants

The first big trade of the 2026 NFL season came back at the end of September.

When the New York Giants lost quarterback Jaxson Dart to a knee injury, many wondered if the team would swing a trade for a quarterback.

Enter J.J. McCarthy. With the former Michigan passer on the losing end of a camp battle with Kyler Murray — and relegated to the QB3 spot to begin the year behind Carson Wentz — he found a fresh start in the Big Apple. And he has taken over as the team’s starting quarterback, leading the Giants to wins over Houston and Philadelphia over the past two games.

Here are the full terms of the trade:

  • Giants receive: QB J.J. McCarthy
  • Vikings receive: A 2027 fifth-round pick

item.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: RBs in timeshares you can trust in Week 10 lineups
item.description: Fantasy analyst Fred Zinkie takes a look at some unsettled backfields across the NFL to see who could be lineup option in Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
Let's take a look at the backup RBs who have a Yahoo roster rate under 60% and could help fantasy teams to victory in Week 10. Players are ranked in order of their Week 10 appeal, and their current roster rates are listed in parentheses.

1. Corey Kiner, Patriots (4%)

Each week, Kiner becomes more appealing. Things continued to trend in his direction in Week 9, starting with information leading up to the game that TreVeyon Henderson is dealing with neurological symptoms. The absence of Henderson pushed Kiner up to the RB2 position, and he averaged 6.9 yards on eight carries in a lopsided loss to the Packers.

The second-year pro has averaged over 5.0 yards per carry in four of the Patriots past five games, while starter Rhamondre Stevenson is averaging just 3.9 yards per carry this season. Comparing the two players for Week 10 is a moot point, since Stevenson is expected to miss time with a knee injury. Kiner is a RB2 option for a potential shootout against the Lions, and he could carve out a permanent role by the time Stevenson returns.

2. Audric Estime, Saints (4%)

With Kendre Miller off the roster and Alvin Kamara past the point in his career where he can handle a heavily workload, Estime was the lead runner in a dramatic Week 9 win over the Browns. The 23-year-old collected 72 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries, while ceding most of the passing game work to Kamara.

The Saints have been quiet on the progress of Travis Etienne Jr., who has been on injured reserve since suffering a hamstring strain in Week 3. Etienne's 21-day practice window has yet to be opened, which means that Estime could handle a heavy workload once again in Week 10, when the Saints host a Panthers team that has allowed the second-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs. Estime is a borderline RB2 for that game.

3. Kaelon Black, 49ers (39%)

At this point, it's undeniable that Kaelon Black has a significant role in the 49ers offense. The rookie gained 70 yards on 11 carries in a lopsided Week 9 win over the Raiders, while starter Christian McCaffrey continued to receive a heavy workload that was divided between the rushing and passing game.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan has compensated for multiple WR injuries by maximizing the use of his RBs, and Black has responded by averaging 4.5 yards per carry. Black's lack of involvement in the passing game limits his upside, but he still carries some flex appeal into a Week 10 matchup against a porous Cowboys defense that has allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs.

4. Seth McGowan, Colts (32%)

This is a big day for McGowan, who could be the Colts starting RB by 4 p.m. ET. And even if Jonathan Taylor remains with the Colts, there seems to be a role for McGowan, who scored and gained 45 yards on six carries in Week 9. McGowan is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in his rookie season and has averaged six carries in his past six games. Meanwhile, Taylor's snap share has consistently dipped throughout the campaign, going from 85% or higher in the initial three games to below 70% in each of the past two contests.

The Colts could continue to move in a run-heavy direction thanks to the disappointing results from Daniel Jones. A Week 10 home game against the low-scoring Dolphins would certainly be a good opportunity to play it safe with a heavy dose of Taylor and McGowan. And if Taylor is traded on Tuesday, McGowan will become an RB2 option for that game.

5. Bam Knight, Cardinals (12%)

Tyler Allgeier came crashing back to earth after his memorable Week 8 performance, as the Seahawks defense held him to 46 total yards on 17 carries and two catches. The Cardinals coaching staff never really expected Allgeier to be the lead back in the first place, as they have often commented that he is best suited for a complementary role that includes significant usage in the passing game. With Jeremiyah Love on IR, Knight is well-positioned to lead the Cardinals in Week 10 carries, provided that he is ready to return from a concussion. Still, his upside is limited, given that the Cardinals have an unsettled QB situation and could be playing from behind against the Rams.

6. Kaleb Johnson, Packers (1%)

Josh Jacobs will almost certainly miss Week 10 and may land on IR while he recovers from surgery on a fractured finger that he suffered in a Week 9 win over the Patriots. With the Packers leading and Jacobs unavailable, they turned to Johnson to put the game away on the ground. Johnson responded by gaining 68 yards on 14 carries and scoring a touchdown in the team's surprising 45-point outburst. As per usual, he was not involved in the passing game, as those responsibilities were handled by Pierre Strong Jr.

With four teams on a bye and others dealing with injuries, Johnson is a strong flex option if MarShawn Lloyd misses a second straight game. The situation becomes more jumbled if Lloyd plays this week, as both he and Johnson would be weak flex options. The value of any Packers RB for Week 10 is also capped by a tough matchup against a Vikings defense that has allowed the eighth-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing running backs.

7. Dylan Sampson, Browns (28%)

A change at QB didn't impact Sampson's role, as the change-of-pace back gained 48 total yards on eight carries and three catches in a Week 9 loss to the Saints. Sampson has 15 carries and 12 catches in three games since returning from IR, as he is clearly the RB who dominates passing game work over Quinshon Judkins. The Browns are underdogs in Week 10 against the Texans, and Sampson could score 5-10 points in PPR formats if they spend most of the game playing from behind.

8. Chris Rodriguez Jr., Jaguars (33%)

Although Bhayshul Tuten has taken over as Jacksonville's lead back, he and Rodriguez have had similar success on the ground. After all, both players have scored four rushing touchdowns, while Tuten is averaging 4.3 yards per carry, in comparison to 4.1 yards for Rodriguez. If the recent usage continues in Week 10, Rodriguez will have roughly half as many carries as Tuten and will have little usage in the passing game. But with the Jaguars heading into a potentially lopsided matchup with the Titans, there could ample opportunity for both rushers.

9. Keaton Mitchell, Chargers (21%)

Mitchell continued to fill the change-of-pace role in Week 9. The speedster ranked third among Los Angeles RBs in snap share, but he was more involved in the passing game than Omarion Hampton or Kimani Vidal.

The 0-8 Chargers are a mess offensively, and they are unlikely to turn things around in Baltimore on Monday Night Football. Still, those in PPR formats can expect 5-8 points from Mitchell, which may be the best available option for some managers in deep leagues.

10. Emmett Johnson, Chiefs (31%)

Although Johnson is showing strong skills as a rookie, he is locked into a low-volume backup role behind superstar Kenneth Walker III. Still, the rookie managed to score a touchdown and gain 34 yards on six carries in a lopsided Week 9 win over the Jets. He could have a role in Week 10, when the Chiefs face a mediocre Falcons defense that has allowed the seventh-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs.

10 Backup RBs to Stash

The players listed below are unlikely to provide significant assistance in Week 10 but are an injury away from having significant value.

  1. Kenny Gainwell, Buccaneers (bye week)

  2. Samaje Perine, Bengals

  3. Justice Hill, Ravens

  4. Mike Washington Jr., Raiders

  5. Tyler Goodson, Cowboys (injured)

  6. Tyjae Spears, Titans

  7. Ray Davis, Bills

  8. Elijah Mitchell, Eagles (bye week)

  9. Kimani Vidal, Chargers

  10. Austin Ekeler, Commanders

Injured Backups to Stash

  • RJ Harvey, Broncos

  • Jonathon Brooks, Panthers

  • Tyrone Tracy Jr., Giants

  • Brian Robinson Jr., Falcons

item.title: Cardinals add QB Joey Aguilar off Jaguars' practice squad

item.content:encoded:
After trading quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and then losing his replacement Gardner Minshew to a potentially season-ending elbow injury, the Cardinals are bringing in quarterback reinforcements.

Joey Aguilar will join the Cardinals' 53-player roster from the Jaguars' practice squad, according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.

The 25-year-old Aguilar was the starting quarterback for the Tennessee Volunteers last season and spent a total of seven years in college football, with two at City College of San Francisco, two at Diablo Valley College and two at Appalachian State before transferring to Tennessee.

The only healthy quarterback in Arizona right now is rookie Carson Beck. Aguilar will presumably back him up on Sunday against the Rams, and the Cardinals will likely add another quarterback to their practice squad or active roster this week.

item.title: Detroit Lions Kerby Joseph won’t play in Germany
item.description: Kerby Joseph isn’t expected to be ready to play in Week 10, but he still has time to return this season.
item.content:encoded:
On Tuesday morning, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell held his weekly interview with local sports radio station 97.1 The Ticket. When discussing the recovery progress of All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph, Campbell said that he doesn’t expect Joseph to be able to play in Week 10 against the New England Patriots in Germany.

“I’ll cut it out (the speculation). I don’t see him playing. I don’t see him playing in Germany,” Campbell told 97.1, per Will Burchfield.

Joseph injured his knee in 2025 during training camp, and limped through the first month of the season before succumbing to his injury. For just over a year, Joseph underwent rehabilitation, working to build strength in his knee. In late October, Joseph finally gained enough stability in his knee to start practicing once again and started his 21-day injury evaluation clock.

Over the last two weeks of practices, Joseph has slowly ramped up his participation levels, as he acclimates back to football activities. On Monday, Campbell said Joseph continues to make progress; they like where he is at and hope to get him even more involved this week.

“He did a good job last week, so we want to get him some more work.”

While Joseph is steadily improving, the early decision to keep him out of Sunday’s game overseas may seem premature, but for a player who hasn’t played in well over a year, it’s not unusual and shouldn’t necessarily be viewed as a negative regarding his progress. Campbell also noted on Monday, when discussing the trade for Andre Cisco, that he expected Joseph to return this season and would give the Lions’ secondary some flexibility.

“We get Kerby back eventually here. Kerby gives you flexibility, keep him where you need him or move him back and forth.“

The Lions don’t want to rush Joseph back into game action, but they are working against the injury evaluation clock, which expires on Tuesday, November 17. At that time, the Lions will need to activate Joseph to the active roster, or they can elect to keep him on the PUP list, which would end his season. If activated, Joseph could potentially return to the field in Week 11 when the Lions host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

item.title: Report: Bengals acquire edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie from Eagles for ‘27 6th-round pick
item.description: The Bengals have made a trade! I repeat, the Bengals have made a trade!
item.content:encoded:
The Cincinnati Bengals have heard your pleas to be active before the trade deadline at 4 PM ET on Tuesday afternoon. According to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, the Bengals have traded away a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie.

Ebiketie was selected in the second round, No. 38 overall, by the Atlanta Falcons in the 2022 NFL Draft out of Penn State. He recorded his first sack in his very first professional game and worked his way into the Falcons’ starting lineup by halfway through his rookie year.

After his rookie contract, he signed a one-year deal with the Eagles this past offseason. Now the Eagles are riddled with injuries, sit at 2-7, and are shedding contracts in exchange for draft picks.

This is clearly a move the Bengals made in response to the injury that landed rookie edge rusher Cashius Howell on IR. It also is a clear signal the Bengals lack trust in their 2025 first-round pick, Shemar Stewart, who only played 10 snaps on Sunday in Spain.

Ebiketie hasn’t made any sacks so far this season, but he has racked up 10 pressures, per PFF. He’ll be a rotational asset for the Bengals’ defensive line, and will join Stewart and Cedric Johnson behind Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy.

Stay tuned for new possible trade news as we near the deadline.

item.title: The Vikings, as expected, are making calls about adding a quarterback
item.description: The clock is ticking, and it won't be cheap to trade for a starter.
item.content:encoded:
They did it in 2016, after Teddy Bridgewater suffered a season-ending knee injury in late August. They did it in 2023, after Kirk Cousins suffered a season-ending torn Achilles tendon.

They're doing it today, in order to avoid having the season end at 6-11.

According to ESPNFL, the Vikings have begun making calls regarding a possible trade for a quarterback.

Of course they're making calls. Coach Kevin O'Connell made that fairly clear last night. The real question is whether they can get a deal done.

They're not operating from a position of strength, especially after a horrendous showing from Carson Wentz, whose passer rating against Buffalo was 8.9. The greater a team's perceived need, the more the other team will want.

The Vikings' best hope is to stumble into a situation where multiple teams are looking to unload a starter. By persuading one team that the Vikings will strike a deal with another team, the price could come down.

There aren't many current starters who would even possibly be available. Two of them — Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and Colts quarterback Daniel Jones — have experience in Minnesota. Others include, potentially, Jets quarterback Geno Smith and Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert.

Backups could be available. Mac Jones had been linked to Minnesota in the past. The 49ers would have to feel comfortable with the alternative to Mac Jones as the understudy to Brock Purdy. If a team trades its No. 2, it assumes the risk that the starter will get injured in the very next game.

That happened to the Steelers in 2019. They traded Josh Dobbs to the Jaguars after Nick Foles was injured in Week 1. In Week 2, the Steelers lost Ben Roethlisberger for the year. Then came the Duck Hodges show.

At this point, it's fair to wonder whether a quarterback upgrade will even matter for the Vikings. The flaws in the offense may run deeper than the quarterback position.

Still, it's obvious that they need someone who can perform more efficiently than Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz, who in all fairness should be cut today.

And if the Vikings can't upgrade at quarterback, they need to listen to offers for receiver Justin Jefferson. His prime is being wasted, and he surely would love to move on (even if he'd never say that out loud).

The last-ditch effort could be to sign Jimmy Garoppolo, who would likely be an instant upgrade to the very low bar that Minnesota's current quarterbacks have established.

item.title: Jerry Jones shares Cowboys plans for NFL trade deadline day
item.description: The Cowboys already swung a major, in-season trade for Joey Porter Jr., but that may all they do before the 2026 NFL trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones does not expect his team to make a major move ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline.

Jones was asked point-blank about Dallas' trade deadline plans during a Tuesday, Nov. 10, interview on 105.3 The Fan. Per usual, the 84-year-old wouldn't categorically rule out a trade, but he cast doubt on whether the Cowboys would swing any deal of significance.

"It's really not ringing, which you've heard me say numerous times," Jones said, referencing a proverbial phone to field trade calls. "That's when you make a trade."

"Don't count it out, a lot of things happen on this last day," he added. "But I don't look for us to make a significant trade today."

Jones' comments come with the Cowboys off to a disappointing 4-5 record start to the 2026 NFL season. They were expected to be NFC East contenders, but their defense has remained a major problem, ranking 30th in defensive EPA per play this season, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats.

Even so, Jones wasn't willing to blame Dallas' middling first half of the 2026 campaign for influencing the team's trade deadline strategy.

"I don't know. I can't answer that," Jones replied when asked if Dallas' performance to date was impacting their status as potential trade deadline buyers. "I haven't had a chance to really maneuver or think about or discuss back and forth with the team. We haven't had a chance to have a meaningful dialogue over the last two or three weeks about any player that we'd be interested in."

While the Cowboys may be quiet at the trade deadline, they did make an aggressive, in-season move to trade for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Porter has appeared in four games for Dallas since that trade, recording eight tackles, three pass defenses and allowing a 39.6 passer rating, per Pro Football Focus.

The Cowboys also made another preseason deal with the Steelers to acquire offensive tackle Broderick Jones, who has played just 43 offensive snaps thus far in 2026 while serving as a swing tackle.

Still, Dallas' 2026 trade deadline plans are a far cry from their 2025 activity, when they acquired star defensive lineman Quinnen Williams from the New York Jets and veteran linebacker Logan Wilson from the Cincinnati Bengals.

item.title: Chargers Power Rankings Roundup: It’s getting lonely at the bottom
item.description: The Chargers remain in the basement of the NFL with little to no company at the bottom.
item.content:encoded:
Following Week Nine, the Chargers remain the only winless team in the NFL.

The Tennessee Titans are right there with just one win this season, but then you look at the remaining 30 teams in the league, each one has multiple wins this year. The Chargers aren’t just the worst team this year, there’s a sizable game between them and the 30th-worst team at the moment.

That fact is remains reflected in this week’s power rankings roundup. As much as I wish there was some sort of change this week, you just can’t with a fat zero in the win column.

If you’re still reading up to this point, thank you, but here’s where the Bolts stand after nine weeks.

ESPN – #32

“At this point, the Chargers are playing for draft position, so, of course, their most important game is against the team on their schedule closest to dethroning them for the No. 1 pick in 2027. Right now, projections say the Chargers will get the No. 1 pick 53% of the time if they lose to Miami in Week 16, but only 21% of the time if they beat the Dolphins.” – Aaron Schatz

Yahoo Sports – #32

“The offseason hiring of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has been a bust. Brought in to ramp things up on that side of the ball, he’s actually done the opposite, with the team averaging a league-worst 15.1 PPG. The defense has also regressed from the 2025 season, currently the 29th-ranked scoring defense, allowing 27.4 PPG.” – Frank Schwab

CBS Sports – #32

“The losing continues and it seems to be getting worse. Will there be changes coming? Should Jim Harbaugh go?” – Pete Prisco

Pro Football Talk – #32

“Do they know they’re winless?” – Mike Florio

The Athletic – #32

“This might’ve been the easiest grade to hand out. The Chargers’ nightmare season continues. Jim Harbaugh’s team has a point differential of minus-98. No other team is worse than the Cardinals’ minus-77. Oh, and their season started with Super Bowl dreams.” – Josh Kendall and Chad Graff

Bleacher Report – #32

“The Los Angeles Chargers have looked and played like the worst team in the NFL since the beginning of the season, and it’s hard to envision things changing in the immediate future.”

“The Chargers’ offense continues to flounder under the direction of Mike McDaniel, and injuries aren’t helping. Ladd McConkey missed another game due to injury, and now Justin Herbert is dealing with a finger injury on his non-throwing hand.”

“Los Angeles’ defense, meanwhile, has looked like a poor imitation of last year’s playoff-caliber unit.“

“The Chargers were just blown out by a Houston Texans squad that has also underwhelmed, though they did find the end zone for the first time since Week 5.” – Kris Knox

Sports Illustrated – #32

“It’s wild that the Chargers are blaming almost everyone else for this utter collapse…except for the coordinator and the quarterback.” – Conor Orr

item.title: Fantasy Football Panic Meter: Matthew Stafford heads to Coping Corner after Puka Nacua injury
item.description: Ray Garvin highlights the concern level for 6 players for fantasy football going into Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
At this point in the season, we have to adjust our expectations. Some of these players still belong in your fantasy football lineup, but that doesn't mean you should feel good about them. The categories remain No Panic, Some Panic, Total Panic and Coping Corner. Nobody here gets No Panic from me.

Jonathan Taylor, RB, Colts: Total Panic if he stays

If Jonathan Taylor stays in Indianapolis, I have total panic. Total panic.

Over the last two games, Taylor has combined for 21 carries, 69 rushing yards and no touchdowns. With two lost fumbles, he's averaged 5.8 half-PPR points. His carries dropped from 21 and 18 in Weeks 6 and 7 to 8 and 13 in Weeks 8 and 9.

He was productive in those earlier games. This hasn't been a month of nothing. But the direction should concern everybody who has Taylor.

I'm watching this usage and wondering whether the Colts are holding him back for a trade. I don't know that. I do know I want him out of there.

I don't trust this offense with Daniel Jones. Indianapolis also traded Quenton Nelson, its All-Pro guard and, in everyone's opinion, its best offensive lineman.

Taylor is a running back who can catch passes. He is not a pass-catching weapon who plays running back. His nine catches over the last two games produced 42 yards. That hasn't come close to rescuing him from bad rushing days.

And I expect the Colts to spend plenty of time trailing. That's a problem when the passing game isn't giving their best offensive player much help.

I'd love a move that gives Taylor a chance to thrive. If he's banished to this offense, we should be very, very concerned.

Chase Brown, RB, Bengals: Some Panic

Every week, there's another reason to believe the Chase Brown game is coming. The receiving work. The offense. The matchup. Then we're disappointed again.

Brown hasn't scored a rushing touchdown since Week 1. That's seven games and 87 carries. He hasn't scored a receiving touchdown or reached 100 rushing yards in a game this season either. He's averaged 8.6 half-PPR points over his last four appearances. Cincinnati scored at least 31 points in all four. This offense is producing. Brown just isn't getting enough of the fantasy payoff.

Joe Burrow is playing at an MVP level with 23 passing touchdowns. The Bengals have five rushing touchdowns as a team. This offense runs through Burrow. Brown can help with dump-offs when Cincinnati is chasing points, but those receiving spikes are hard to predict. He caught eight passes in Week 8 and three the following week.

Chase Brown is who he is.

I've got Some Panic because I know what I'm getting: a volatile mid-to-low-end RB2 with sporadic receiving upside. I'm done treating every week like the breakout is right around the corner.

Derrick Henry, RB, Ravens: Total Panic

I talked about this on the Yahoo Data Dump show. I've been concerned about Derrick Henry.

The crown has fallen. He is no longer the king.

Henry is 32, and Father Time always wins. Give him a runway and he can still get north and south quickly. But I'm not seeing him make defenders miss the way this offense needs him to, and I think this offensive line has been dreadful. The season totals look fine until you're actually living with these afternoons.

Seven of his eight rushing touchdowns came in the first four weeks. Over his last four games, Henry has 62 carries for 213 yards and one rushing touchdown. That's 3.4 yards per carry. He's added four catches for 13 yards.

Baltimore scored 10, 13, 10 and 10 points in those games. Its last three losses were all by at least 20 points. The defense isn't keeping games close, and the offense isn't creating enough scoring opportunities.

Could Jacoby Brissett help? Sure. Jesse Minter says Brissett is going to start in Week 10. But I need to see it. Brissett doesn't immediately fix the blocking, the defense or my concerns about Henry himself. Total Panic. You're playing him as a mid-to-low-end RB2 right now.

Jayden Daniels, QB, Commanders: Some Panic

The only reason Jayden Daniels isn't in Total Panic is that my expectations have been adjusted. I hope yours have, too. He returned from the elbow injury in Week 5 and ran for 103 yards and two touchdowns. The rushing alone gave you 22.3 fantasy points.

Since then, he has 10 carries for 49 yards and no rushing touchdowns across three games. That's about 1.6 fantasy points per game from rushing.

The passing hasn't completely fallen apart. Daniels threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns in Week 6. But his last two fantasy scores were 14.98 and 14.56. Without the rushing advantage, there's much less room for an ordinary passing performance.

Terry McLaurin is out for the season, and Washington doesn't have many pass-catching options to replace him. The margin for success is smaller.

I've got Some Panic because I'm no longer expecting Daniels to automatically give me the advantage I drafted him for. If there's a better weekly streaming option, I'm considering it. He's no longer a must-play quarterback for me.

Matthew Stafford, QB, Rams: Coping Corner

I have total, total panic about this situation. Matthew Stafford belongs in Coping Corner. He wasn't giving us enough with Puka Nacua. Now, Puka is likely headed to injured reserve with MCL and PCL sprains along with turf toe. Stafford has averaged 200.5 passing yards and 13.47 fantasy points over his last four games. He hasn't reached 250 passing yards in any of them. His last two fantasy scores were 8.28 and 11.22.

We were already talking ourselves into starting him. Now, we're taking away his best receiving option. Head coach Sean McVay expects Davante Adams back toward the shorter end of his 6-10 week window. But what does "sooner" mean for your lineup right now?

Stafford is 38, and to me, he's showing his age. His right elbow was on the Week 9 injury report, although he practiced fully. I can't tell you the elbow explains everything, but this situation gives me little confidence.

With Puka, Stafford was streamable. Without Puka and Davante, he's a quarterback I have zero interest in starting.

Drake London, WR, Falcons: Total Panic

Drake London is in Total Panic, too. Michael Penix Jr. has not been good. This offense has not been good. London is still Atlanta's leading receiver, but that doesn't make me feel better about the situation.

Over his last four games, London has 17 catches for 204 yards and one touchdown, averaging 8.7 half-PPR points. Over the last two, he has six catches for 76 yards and no touchdowns.

Penix has combined for 287 passing yards, one touchdown and five interceptions across those two games. How much confidence are we supposed to have in London delivering WR1 production in that environment? London has 692 receiving yards this season, so there have been productive games. But he has one receiving touchdown, and this recent connection hasn't been good enough.

You drafted him in the first round to be your WR1. This isn't close to what you needed.

I have low faith in Penix right now, and that directly affects how I feel about London.

The talent hasn't changed. My confidence in this offense consistently getting that talent into your fantasy lineup has. I'm not comfortable pretending the situation is fine.

Total Panic.

Today is the 51st anniversary of the sinking of the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald into Lake Superior, as it was steaming towards Detroit with a load of iron ore pellets in its hull.

Today is also a Tuesday, when the film reviews, analyses and breakdowns of the game are posted, and there are some informative ones in the links below. No lives were lost in this past Sunday’s disaster for the Patriots, but more players added to an already-too-long list of injured players. I’m not ready to declare the roster a sinking ship yet though.

This also happens to be the NFL trade deadline, today at 4:00 pm ET. I’ve heard many fans bemoaning the fact that the front office isn’t doing anything to try and add pieces to patch up the roster. My opinion is that there are simply too many holes in this boat to fix with a trade – that won’t also break the bank of cap space or future draft assets. If the issue is shoring up one position, then the price may be worth it to sail on to the playoffs. But where would the Patriots even start? OL? RB? WR? The list is too long. My hope is that some injured players start to return to help the team stack up some wins – but I don’t want to see the team jettison draft picks for a quick fix that may or may not even work out.
