item.title: Liam Coen: "Definitely a curve" to getting Jessie Bates ready this week
item.description: The Jaguars made three trades on Monday, but their deal for safety Jessie Bates was the only one that was completed when head coach Liam Coen met with reporters on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars made three trades on Monday, but their deal for safety Jessie Bates was the only one that was completed when head coach Liam Coen met with reporters on Monday.

Coen called it a "no-brainer" to make a trade for a player who has shown the "ability to see things before they happen" on the field while also serving as a team captain in the locker room. Bates has been honing those skills for nine seasons, so he's gained quite a bit of experience but Coen said it will still be "definitely a curve" in terms of getting him acclimated to the Jaguars defense on the fly.

"You've seen it done so many ways, right? So many different examples of it being done," Coen said. "I know he's pretty intelligent, and he'll be able to understand a lot of that. It's more the checks and balances right in between plays, the communication from two by two to three by one, the motions, the checks. Like our verbiage where I would imagine three, cover three, cover four, you know, like the coverages, he'll understand and know and be able to play those, line up and play. It's more of the checks and balances and things that go into each play that we'll have to work through. We'll take it one day at a time, see what happens."

Defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux are the other new members of the Jaguars defense and the team's staff will be working overtime this week to make sure all of them are up to speed in time to face the Titans on Sunday.

item.title: Vikings vs. Packers odds: Vikings underdogs heading into Lambeau
item.description: Totally unsurprising, to say the least
item.content:encoded:
After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division’s basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don’t like their chances.

Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday’s game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points.

The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher.

The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that’s just how good the NFC North has been this season.

These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start.

With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don’t do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

item.title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 10
item.description: The Giants creep closer to the top 10.
item.content:encoded:
No. 1 — Buffalo Bills (6-1) | SAME

A defensive effort in which the Bills stopped the Vikings’ Carson Wentz-led offense, while Josh Allen and the offense did enough to secure a pivotal road victory against Minnesota.

No. 2 — Chicago Bears (7-2) | SAME

Caleb Williams started in his typical efficient self, and it looked like he could do no wrong, but then he proceeded to throw four interceptions, and the Bears’ offense stagnated for much of the game after taking a 17-3 lead. The Buccaneers made the game interesting, forcing five turnovers, but Chicago held strong and defeated Tampa Bay, 27-24.

No. 3 — San Fransico 49ers (7-1) | SAME

Brock Purdy went 17 of 25 for 232 yards with a pair of touchdowns to help the 49ers defeat the Las Vegas Raiders, 38-17. The Raiders kept the game interesting up until about half-time, but the 49ers scored two touchdowns in the third quarter to pull away from the Raiders. The defense forced an insane five turnovers. San Francisco remains a top team in the NFL.

No. 4 —Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) | SAME

Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the NFL, but they faced a Joe Fagnano’s Ravens team that only scored 10 points. Jacksonville won the game 33-10 and Trevor Lawrence only completed 16 passes. The Jaguars are an excellent young football team playing complementary football. 

No. 5 — Denver Broncos (7-2) | (6th) 📈 1 spot

Denver found a way to earn a tough road win, again! Pat Bryant returned from IR and caught a touchdown from Bo Nix. Jonah Coleman continues to dominate touches as the team’s No. 1 back. Coleman had 17 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown in the game. 

No. 6 — Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) | (6th) 📈 3 spots

The Bengals offense is playing very well. Joe Burrow tossed three touchdowns and 271 yards against the Falcons. Ja’Marr Chase caught ten passes for 155 yards with a touchdown. The rushing attack is still a work in progress for Cincinnati, but the Bengals have now won four games in a row, scoring over 30 points in each matchup.

No. 7 —Minnesota Vikings (6-2) | (5th) 📉 2 spots

The Minnesota Vikings battled the Bills but lost at home to Josh Allen. The Carson Wentz experience was not enjoyable, as he threw several interceptions and could not move the offense. Minnesota still has the best defense — and possibly the best unit overall — but this offense is bad.

No. 8 —Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) | 📉 1 spot

Kansas City got right against the Jets in a 35-12 victory. Patrick Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards with a pair of touchdowns, and Kenneth Walker III rushed for over 100 yards with both receiving touchdowns. The Chiefs dominated an inferior opponent. 

No. 9 — Detroit Lions (6-2) | (8th) 📉 1 spot

Detroit went into Miami and won a gritty game that relied on defensive football. Each team turned the football over once, and neither team earned 300 yards on offense. Kudos to Miami’s defense, but the Dolphins were a fish out of water for the Lions in Miami.

No. 10 — Green Bay Packers (6-3) | 📈 3 spots

The Green Bay Packers demolished the New England Patriots in their home. They forced four turnovers and gained 478 yards of offense. Jordan Love played out of his MIND, completing 23 of 29 for 372 yards and three touchdowns. Few teams are hotter than the Packers right now, and their defense matched their offense in New England. Green Bay did, however, lose running back Josh Jacobs to a broken finger. The Packers still have concerns, but Love is playing at an MVP rate.

No. 11 — Seattle Seahawks (5-4) | (SAME

Drew Lock is 2-0 this season for Seattle; he completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in this low-scoring 17-3 win over Arizona. Seattle travels to Las Vegas to play the Raiders before going into a bye week. 

No. 12— Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) | SAME

The Pittsburgh Steelers were on their bye in Week 9.

No. 13 —New York Giants (5-2-1) | (15th) 📈 2 spots

The Giants continue to win football games because they’re well coached in every phase. The defense pressured and harassed Joe Milton all game, sacking the young quarterback seven times, while Matt Nagy called a fine game for multiple quarterback. Jameis Winston led the only touchdown drive against Vic Fangio’s defense. The Giants earned their first win in Philadelphia since 2013.

No. 14 — Los Angeles Rams (5-4) | SAME

The Rams defeated Washington 20-13 on the road, but lost their star receiver Puka Nacua in the last play of the game. Los Angeles is a good team that is well coached, but injuries are stacking up, and a lack of offensive playmakers is problematic. They may receive Terrance Ferguson back soon, but Matt Stafford is losing targets weekly.

No. 15 — New England Patriots (5-4) | (10th) 📉 5 spots

The Patriots were embarrassed by the Packers, 45-27. They’re an injured squad at receiver and Drake Maye tossed three interceptions and was harassed throughout the game. It was a tough look for New England on defense – they surrendered a surprising 478 yards to Jordan Love and the Packers.

No. 16 — Houston Texans (3-5) | (20th) 📈 4 spots

The Texans came off the bye week and blew the Chargers out, 44-22. C.J. Stroud went nuclear, finishing 21 of 35 for 384 yards with five touchdowns and a pick. Kayshon Boutte went four for 125 and two; Tank Dell four of 105 for one, and Nico Collins four for 55 with one as well.  Houston played to their talent against the worst team in the league.

No. 17 — Cleveland Browns (5-3) | (16th) 📉 1 spot

Cleveland lost 23-22 in overtime. Shedeur Sanders went 19 of 31 for 297 yards with two touchdowns with exceptional individual efforts from Harold Fannin Jr. and KC Concepcion on the two 64 and 39 yard touchdown passes. Tyler Shough turned it on down the stretch of the game and the Saints found a way to secure victory at the end of the game. Cleveland has a decision to make next week – Sanders or DeShaun Watson?

No. 18 — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-4) | (17th) 📉 1 spot

Tampa Bay has won two games in a row and three of four. The Bucs won last week without completing a pass. They’re a power-run team with an opportunistic, well-coached defense, but the Bears withstood a valiant come-from-behind effort. Tampa Bay lost 27-24.

No. 19 — Baltimore Ravens (5-5) | (20th) 📈 1 spot

Baltimore lost to Jacksonville, 33-10, but they were forced to start Joe Fagnano, who went 10 of 18 for 60 yards. Baltimore had a creative game plan centered around the wildcat, but Jacksonville was too much in the second half. Baltimore traded for Jacoby Brissett, who should start in Week 10. 

No. 20 — Carolina Panthers (3-5) | (19th) 📉 1 spot

Bryce Young played well against a good defense, completing 28 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns, but as the Broncos do – they found a way to win, 26-21. The Panthers are now 3-5 with three straight losses.

No. 21 — Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) | (18th) 📉 3 spots

The Raiders turned the football over five times, with three of them being Kirk Cousins interceptions. Brock Bowers caught seven passes for 111 yards with a touchdown on eight targets. The Raiders can’t beat a team like San Francisco on the road while throwing three picks and putting the ball on the ground three more times (two of which were recovered by the other team).

No. 22 — New Orleans Saints (3-5)| (23rd) 📈 1 spot

Tyler Shough led a fourth-quarter comeback to force overtime and finished the game 21 of 35 for 265 yards with a touchdown and 51 yards on the ground. Audric Estime, who was on the Browns’ practice squad last week, rushed for 72 yards and a touchdown for the Saints.

No. 23 — Atlanta Falcons (3-6) | (22nd) 📉 1 spot

Atlanta has lost four of the last five games, this one in Madrid, Spain. The quarterback play is sub-par; Michael Penix Jr. threw for just 162 yards in the game, and Drake London took a bit to get going. Atlanta is in a bad division, and they’re a team that struggles to establish an identity. 

No. 24 — Dallas Cowboys (4-5) | (25th) 📈 1 spot

Dallas has talent on both sides of the football, but they’re a mess. Dak Prescott, though, did complete 21 of 34 for 335 yards and a pair of touchdowns against a Colts team that is in a fire sale. Dallas, somehow, almost lost this game and found a way to win late 27-23. The Cowboys are one of the biggest disappointment teams in the 2026 season, which is just lovely.

No. 25 — Washington Commanders (3-4-1)| (26th) 📈 1 spot

Jayden Daniels completed 24 of 35 passes for 274 yards with a touchdown pass to Van Jefferson, but that wasn’t enough to defeat the Los Angeles Rams, who earned this road win, 20-13. Washington’s offense has struggled and the Commanders’ rushing attack remained bad in this game.

No. 26 — New York Jets (2-7) | (27th) 📈 1 spot

The Jets went to Kansas City and lost, 35-12. They did little offensively, converting 2 of 14 third and fourth down conversions. They couldn’t stop the run on defense. Aaron Glenn’s time as a head coach may be coming to an end.

No. 27 — Arizona Cardinals, (3-6) | (26th) 📉 3 spots

Gardner Minshew II couldn’t do much against Mike Macdonald’s defense in this 3-17 loss. Minshew was then hurt and it looks like Arizona will turn to Carson Beck, now that Jacoby Brissett was traded to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona is down love, multiple quarterbacks, and Michael Wilson was placed on IR. Not good!

No. 28 — Miami Dolphins (1-7)| SAME

Miami played well since their bye week, but could only muster nine points against Detroit. Malik Willis finished 13 of 25 for just 128 yards with an interception. It’s a rebuilding year for Miami. 

No. 29 — Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) | SAME

The Eagles have lost seven straight games and changed to quarterback Joe Milton to try and spark the team at home against the Giants. The defense played with spirit, but the offense was inept, and the rushing attack was stifled by the Giants’ defense. Philadelphia traded Jordan Davis on Monday morning, and they’re looking forward to the off-season.

No. 30 — Tennessee Titans (1-7) | SAME

The Tennessee Titans wereon their bye in Week 9.

No. 31 —Indianapolis Colts (2-7) | SAME

Daniel Jones almost did the Giants a solid by stealing a win in this lost season, but Dallas escaped with a 27-23 victory.

No. 32 — Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) | SAME

The Chargers are terrible. They can’t do anything but score 13 points in garbage time to make the score more respectable. Just an embarrassing season for this franchise.

item.title: Former All-Pro WR seems to wish he played for Liam Coen
item.description: Dez Bryant feels like his career was ‘robbed’ after watching Liam Coen lead the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are 6-2.

I REPEAT:

The Jacksonville Jaguars are 6-2.

Liam Coen has the best regular season winning percentage (0.762) of any head coach in franchise history. He could move into third place in all-time wins by the end of this season. The beginning of the Coen era has been a thorough success.

This week, Coen told his team to stay hungry.

“How great do we really want to be? Because we could sit here and say, ‘Alright, we’re at 6-2, just had a good win.’ OR. We can say, ‘We’re gonna f—ing be great. And I don’t mean on Sunday in a game. I’m talking about today.”

“I’m not asking you to go from good to great in a f—ing day. I’m asking us to go and pursue greatness with a relentless f—ing attack.”

If that doesn’t make you want to run through a brick wall, I don’t know what will.

Coen’s message did fire up a certain former three-time Pro Bowl wide receiver who spent seven of his nine NFL seasons coached by Jason Garrett.

Could you imagine prime Dez Bryant in an offense designed by Coen?!

item.content:encoded:
Will the offense for the Los Angeles Rams run through Blake Corum and Kyren Williams? The running game for L.A. has been a massive part of their 3-game win streak, and with Puka Nacua missing time, they’ll likely need the run game even more. Will they keep using both backs or will one start to get more run than the other?

Sean McVay may be tested to see if he can stay with the run as he and many coaches sometimes abandon the run or don’t use it enough to keep the defense in check. Even if the run game isn’t producing, it can still help take pressure off the quarterback and tire out an opposing defense.

The Rams will need to continue to lean on both backs who can both run, block, catch, and seemingly do whatever the Rams are ask. How well can the run game be without Puka Nacua assisting? Week 10 will be a big test for the Rams and their offense.

They’ll hope their running backs can help steer their team to their fourth win in a row.

Rams PFF grades: Best and worst performers in win vs. Commanders (ramswire)

“Jackson allowed two pressures, but both of them were just hurries and he didn’t give up a QB hit or sack.

Corum forced two missed tackles on his way to rushing for 58 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries. Williams didn’t force any missed tackles but he did have a 71.1 pass-blocking grade.“

Rams trade deadline tracker: Latest rumors, news and buzz (ramswire)

“The Los Angeles Rams went all-in this offseason by trading for Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett, while also adding Jaylen Watson and Aaron Donald on defense. At 5-4, they’re not where they expected to be at the midway point, but the trade deadline offers them a chance to improve before the second half of the season begins.

Teams have until Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET to make any final trades. Sean McVay has indicated the Rams will more or less stand pat, knowing Davante Adams, Kobie Turner and Terrance Ferguson will all be back at some point this season, but plans always change.“

Myles Garrett: ‘I am that closer. We don’t need to look any further’ | ‘The NFL Report’ (nfl.com)

“Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett talks about his impact on the Rams defense.”

3 Wide Receivers the Rams Must Target at NFL Trade Deadline After Puka Nacua Injury (sports.yahoo)

“If the Los Angeles Rams were in need of a wide receiver last week, they will be desperate for one heading into Tuesday’s trade deadline. The Rams will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for at least the next four weeks with a sprained PCL and MCL in his knee. Over the next four weeks, The Rams now enter another grueling stretch of their schedule. If they are going to remain competitive, trading for a wide receiver is a must. Here are three wide receivers the Rams should consider trading for ahead of Tuesday’s deadline.

Brian Thomas Jr., Jacksonville Jaguars

Prior to the Rams losing Puka Nacua, Brian Thomas Jr. may not have made the most sense. It was hard to see where he fit once Davante Adams returned from injury. However, with both Nacua and Adams out, the Rams need a player that has the ability to be a WR1. While Thomas hasn’t found success in Liam Coen’s offense, he has already shown that he can be a WR1. He had 1,200 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie and fits the wide receiver profile that has been successful with Stafford.“

Latest updates on Rams WR Puka Nacua’s knee injury (ramswire)

“McVay provided an update on Nacua Monday, telling reporters that the star receiver will likely be placed on injured reserve with an MCL and PCL sprain, as well as turf toe. If he does go on IR, Nacua won’t be eligible to return until Week 15 at the earliest.”

‘Desperately Need a Trade,’ ‘Take Josh Downs off the Colts’ Hands’ — NFL Fans Urge Rams To Make a Move After Puka Nacua Lands on IR With New Injury (sports.yahoo)

“Replacing Nacua’s production won’t be easy. He caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown before leaving Sunday’s game. He also leads the Rams with 70 receptions for 715 yards this season and ranks No. 6 among wide receivers with a PFN WR Impact Score of 86.0.

With Adams also sidelined, Los Angeles will have to lean on Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, and CJ Daniels at receiver. Tight ends Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson could also take on larger roles in the passing game.

Still, fans want the Rams to look beyond their current options and add another receiver. One supporter made the case for a trade on X, writing, “Now we desperately need a trade.”

NFL Week 9 Sunday aftermath: Myles Garrett’s return buoys Rams; Jordan Love, Joe Burrow shine (nfl.com)

“The NFC North continues to be an absolute buzzsaw of a division, going 3-0 on Sunday with the Vikings set to face the Bills on Monday night. The AFC North is shaping up to be a two-team race, and the Seahawks got back over .500 with Sam Darnold sidelined.

Let’s examine some key storylines in Sunday’s aftermath, including:

  • Prolific Packers attack fueled by deep ball
  • Burrow marching toward first MVP
  • Another one-score win for Payton’s Broncos
  • Giants overcome adversity once again
  • Stroud’s historic afternoon in Los Angeles

But first, we start with the Rams, who saw the return of their prized offseason acquisition and immediately reaped the benefits.“

“How about the defense?!” Sean McVay’s victory speech after Week 9 win vs. Commanders (rams.com)

“Watch Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay’s victory speech after Sunday’s Week 9 win against the Washington Commanders.”

Puka Nacua’s impossible performance and other reactions to Rams’ Week 9 win (ramblinfan)

“The Rams were tested throughout the game. The performance gives coaches plenty to work on in practice, but the team showed plenty of positives as well. Still, an offense that seemed to score at will in 2025 was held in check. If it isn’t fixed, that’s going to be a problem going forward.

5 instant reactions to Rams’ win over Commanders

1. Rams’ offensive inconsistency continues

While the defense competed in Week 9 without both starting cornerbacks, it was the offense that struggled once more. Matthew Stafford was unable to connect consistently with any receiver not named Puka Nacua. The running backs did not rack up huge gains early. And as soon as Los Angeles fell behind, the offense began to pass far too frequently.“

NFL news roundup: J.J. McCarthy expected to play Week 10; Justin Herbert avoids finger fracture (nfl.com)

“WR Puka Nacua is likely to be placed on injured reserve with turf toe and a sprained MCL and PCL, coach Sean McVay said.

OL Steve Avila will miss time with a hamstring strain, per McVay.

CB Trent McDuffie is day to day with his back injury, McVay said.“
